title: AIW rc.10.59 Architecture Design Toolset

authority.source: Governed, pinned rc.10.55 knowledge snapshot plus approved operational claims
authority.limitation: This build normalizes and activates the pinned governed corpus. It does not claim a fresh live extraction and independent promotion run for every public repository.

stages.objective: Frame the problem, intended benefit, stakeholders, scope and constraints.
cambridgeQuestions: What business outcome and intended benefit justify the architecture work?
Who uses, funds, operates, governs and is affected by the solution?
What motivations, wishes and concerns must the architecture address?
What is explicitly in and out of scope?
Which assumptions require validation before synthesis?

stages.objective: Convert outcomes and constraints into measurable ASRs and trade-offs.
cambridgeQuestions: Which requirements are architecturally significant?
Can each quality requirement be written as source, stimulus, environment, artifact, response and response measure?
Which quality drivers conflict, and which trade-off authority decides?
What baseline and measurable target will prove success?

stages.objective: Define vendor-neutral responsibilities, boundaries, data ownership and interactions.
cambridgeQuestions: Which business capabilities and bounded responsibilities belong together?
Where should cohesion be high and coupling low?
Which components own behaviour and data?
What abstractions prevent ripple effects and preserve information hiding?

stages.objective: Realize logical responsibilities as deployable components and explicit contracts.
cambridgeQuestions: Which deployable units realize each logical responsibility?
Which interfaces are required by each consumer and provider?
Which communication patterns are synchronous, asynchronous or batch, and why?
Which pattern obligations become tests or review controls?

stages.objective: Select provider-neutral platform, data, security, integration and observability capabilities.
cambridgeQuestions: Which vendor-neutral capabilities are required?
Which capabilities are mandatory, optional or prohibited by constraints?
What platform, security, data and observability services support the design?

stages.objective: Map neutral capabilities to products, topology, trust zones and recovery paths.
obligations: no vendor override of neutral design
cambridgeQuestions: Which products or managed services realize each accepted capability?
What deployment zones, trust boundaries, scaling units and recovery paths are required?
What provider-specific limits or costs alter the neutral design?

stages.objective: Review completeness, risks, decisions, conformance and readiness.
cambridgeQuestions: Which decisions address which drivers?
What alternatives were rejected and under what counterfactual conditions would they become preferable?
What risks, assumptions and failure modes remain?
Which fitness tests and evidence demonstrate readiness?

stages.objective: Assemble a coherent, audience-specific and traceable architecture delivery pack.
cambridgeQuestions: Which audience needs which viewpoint and level of detail?
Does every significant requirement trace to decisions, components, interfaces and tests?
Are diagrams generated from the same canonical model as the narrative?
What is incomplete, externally dependent or awaiting acceptance?

obligations.title: Layered operating obligation
obligations.description: Define ownership, monitoring, failure handling and review criteria introduced by Layered.
obligations.verificationHint: Confirm the obligation is linked to an owner, a measurable control and an architecture fitness function where possible.

risks: Misapplying Layered can add complexity without improving the priority quality attributes.
antiPatternDetection: Detect required component roles: Application Boundary, Application Core.
Detect required contracts: OpenAPI or typed command, provider-neutral port.
Flag partial adoption when mandatory obligations lack owners or evidence.

conformanceRules.rationale: Preserve the accepted Layered intent in implementation and deployment evidence.

fitnessTests: RULE-LAYERED-01: Conformance for Layered — Preserve the accepted Layered intent in implementation and deployment evidence.
transitionStrategies: Introduce Layered behind a bounded scope and capture a baseline.
Run compatibility and conformance checks before expanding adoption.
Retain a reversible migration or rollback path until evidence is accepted.
providerNeutralRealization: Model responsibilities, contracts, policies and failure behaviour before product selection.
Map provider services only after neutral capabilities and quality obligations are accepted.

approvedClaims.statement: CALM represents architecture patterns as reusable machine-readable constraints that can be validated against concrete architectures.
Immutable event stores can conflict with data-erasure obligations, so sensitive personal data should be separated or protected with a deliberate deletion strategy.
A developer portal catalog should be treated as a synchronized discovery and caching layer rather than the ultimate architecture source of truth.
ArchUnit can turn approved Java architecture dependency and layering decisions into executable unit-test rules.
jQAssistant can scan software artifacts into a graph and evaluate architecture constraints, making it useful for intended-versus-implemented architecture comparison.
OAM separates application workload components from operational traits, policies and workflows, supporting clearer responsibility boundaries.
The DDD starter modelling process combines several collaborative techniques to validate domain boundaries and message flows iteratively.
The OpenTelemetry demo provides a useful test corpus for observability topology, telemetry dependencies and failure-simulation scenarios.

sourceLocations.heading: Welcome to the OpenTelemetry Astronomy Shop Demo

approvedClaims.statement: Service-mesh configurations can be captured as reusable declarative patterns and imported as topology plus policy metadata.
jMolecules can express DDD building blocks, events and architectural styles in code and connect those declarations to ArchUnit or jQAssistant verification.
Spring Modulith can discover and verify application modules, test them independently, observe module interactions and generate documentation from the implemented module arrangement.
Context Mapper DSL provides a machine-readable representation of strategic DDD context maps and service-decomposition models that can be imported into and exported from AIW.
Meshery models and design templates can provide component, relationship and topology metadata for an AIW deployment-view adapter.

sourceLocations.heading: Visually and collaboratively manage your infrastructure

approvedClaims.statement: The CNCF Landscape Graph can enrich AIW technology discovery and taxonomy metadata, but landscape inclusion must not be interpreted as architectural endorsement.

closureBacklog: Link each priority Pattern DNA field to independently reviewed atomic source claims.
Execute live refresh, extraction, contradiction review and independent promotion for approved production connectors.
Deepen provider-product mappings without allowing provider products to override vendor-neutral capability design.
Continue specialist editorial calibration of generated component and interface kits.
